memories.text: ocean is the main Docker host and runs the mem0, Plex and Grafana containers.
node006 is a Proxmox node with 128 GB of RAM and two NVMe drives.
nas01 stores media on a ZFS pool named data01, laid out as RAIDZ2 across eight 16 TB drives.
Two drives in the data01 pool, sdh and sdi, are throwing SMART errors and need replacing.
The homelab DHCP server is Kea, running on the router VM.
Unbound on the pihole box resolves DNS for the homelab and forwards to Quad9.
Cloudflare DDNS updates home.terrac.com every five minutes from a cron job on ocean.
The Cloudflare DDNS API token was rotated after it leaked in a public CI log.
gh-runner-01 hosts four ephemeral self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for the homelab repo.
Homelab deploys are fully CI-mediated; ansible-playbook never runs from the laptop.
Grafana dashboards live on ocean at port 3000 behind the nginx reverse proxy.
Prometheus scrapes node exporters on every host every 30 seconds.
Loki keeps container logs for 14 days.
Loki retention was raised from 14 days to 30 days to debug the mem0 restatement bug.
The UPS in the rack is an APC SMT1500 that gives about 25 minutes of runtime.
Vaultwarden runs on node005 and is backed up nightly to nas01.
Home Assistant controls the office lights and the cat feeder schedule.
The nginx reverse proxy terminates TLS with a wildcard certificate from Let's Encrypt.
ocean ran out of disk on /var/lib/docker, so a nightly image prune timer was added.
mem0 on ocean stores vectors in pgvector in the mem0-postgres container and gets nomic embeddings from mem0-ollama.
mem0 fact extraction uses a frontier model while embeddings stay local at 768 dimensions.
The mem0 recall hook searches with a threshold of 0.45 and a limit of 10 results.
IoT devices live on VLAN 30, which cannot reach the server VLAN.
The office switch is a 10 GbE MikroTik CRS309.
node005 kernel panics were traced to a failing stick of RAM in slot B2.
Backups go to Backblaze B2 with restic every night at 2am.
Restic backups moved from 2am to 4am so they stop overlapping the Tdarr transcode window.
Tailscale connects the laptop to the homelab when travelling.
SSH to every host uses ed25519 keys and password login is disabled.
The ansible vault password file is ~/.ansible_vault_pass with mode 600.
Plex runs on ocean with hardware transcoding on an Intel Arc A380.
The Plex token leaked in a screenshot and was rotated.
Tdarr transcodes the library to HEVC overnight between midnight and 4am.
Sonarr manages TV shows and Radarr manages movies, and both send downloads to NZBGet.
Prowlarr syncs indexers to Sonarr and Radarr.
NZBGet downloads to /mnt/data01/downloads and the arr apps hardlink completed files from there.
The nzbget exporter was added to Prometheus to alert on stalled downloads.
Plex Meta Manager rebuilds collections every Sunday.
Jellyfin was tried as a Plex replacement and dropped because of subtitle problems.
Tdarr GPU workers were cut from three to one because transcodes were starving Plex.
At work I run production Kafka with 12 brokers across three availability zones.
The production Kafka cluster runs in KRaft mode, not ZooKeeper.
Kafka partition rebalances run every second Tuesday, before the weekly release.
Kafka partition rebalances moved to every second Thursday, after the weekly release.
Kafka topic retention is seven days by default and 30 days for the audit topics.
Consumer lag alerts fire when lag passes 50,000 messages for ten minutes.
The Kafka brokers run on i4i instances because of their local NVMe.
A Kafka broker disk filled up in July because tiered storage was misconfigured.
Schema Registry enforces backward compatibility on every topic.
I'm on call for the Kafka platform every fourth week.
I make techno on an Akai MPC One, usually around 132 BPM.
The Elektron Digitakt handles drums and the MPC One sequences everything.
Tracks get mixed down in Ableton Live before mastering.
I'm working on an EP of four tracks called Ocean Floor.
The Ocean Floor EP was cut to three tracks; the fourth moved to a later release.
The studio monitors are Adam A7X speakers on isolation pads.
MPC One projects are backed up to nas01 after every session.
MPC firmware 3.4 broke MIDI clock sync with the Digitakt.
I prefer hardware sequencing over arranging in a DAW.
I'm playing a live techno set at a warehouse party next month.
I have six cats: Miso, Tofu, Biscuit, Pepper, Mochi and Ziggy.
Biscuit only eats salmon pate.
Pepper is on thyroid medication, half a tablet twice a day.
Pepper's thyroid dose went up to a full tablet twice a day after the last blood test.
Ziggy is the youngest cat and knocks things off desks.
Mochi has a sensitive stomach and needs hydrolysed protein food.
The cats' vet is Dr. Alvarez at Riverside Animal Clinic.
Tofu had a dental cleaning and two teeth removed.
The automatic cat feeder runs at 7am and 6pm.
Miso is the oldest cat at 14 and has early kidney disease.
Cat food is ordered monthly in bulk from Chewy.
There are seven litter boxes and they get scooped twice a day.
Every change gets its own git worktree and branch, and one PR each.
PRs only ever target my own repos, never a fork's upstream.
Commits carry only my authorship, with no AI co-author trailers.
PR #16 made the mem0 server read its auth config per request instead of once at import.
PR #15 fixed mem0 dropping corrections as near-duplicates.
PR #593 added the Prometheus scrape config for the nzbget exporter.
PR #595 added the deploy detector to the homelab CI.
PR #422 had a Kea DHCP fix that was salvaged into its own two-file PR.
PR #390 fixed the homelab CI and PR #389 removed unused services.
PR #18 stopped keyword-only search results outranking stronger semantic matches in mem0.
PR #19 raised the mem0 entity boost floor from 0.5 to 0.75.
The homelab repo is the master configuration for the whole fleet.
I prefer rg over grep and fd over find.
Homelab deploys auto-merge on green CI and never auto-rollback.
Reminders and scheduled work stay local, never in cloud schedulers.
I write without em dashes.
The TypeScript SDK is unmaintained in my mem0 fork.
The mem0 fork merges upstream mem0ai/mem0 regularly to stay current with fixes.
I live in Portland and bike to the office.
I drink pour-over coffee from a Chemex every morning.
I'm vegetarian and cook a lot of Thai food.
I have ADD and keep a running todo list to stay on track.
I'm learning Rust by rewriting a log shipper.
My car is a 2019 Subaru Outback, due for its 60,000 mile service.
The Outback's 60,000 mile service is done and the brakes were replaced.
My standing desk is set to 112 cm when standing.
I read science fiction, most recently Ada Palmer's Terra Ignota series.
The garden has tomatoes, basil and far too much mint.
PR #160 bumped the Grafana image to 11.2.
PR #61 fixed a typo in the homelab README.
PR #1600 is an open draft for the Loki storage migration.
Issue #593 tracks flaky SMART alerts on nas01.
Grafana was on 10.4 before the 11.2 upgrade.
node005 runs Proxmox 8.1.
node006 was upgraded to Proxmox 8.2.
Port 8888 on the laptop is the SSH tunnel to the mem0 API on ocean.
Port 8080 on ocean is the Tdarr web UI.
Port 9090 on ocean is Prometheus.
The rack has a 24-port patch panel and every cable is labelled with a Brother P-touch.
Power draw for the whole rack averages 420 watts.
Electricity is the biggest homelab cost, about 45 dollars a month.
The homelab runbook lives in docs/operations in the homelab repo.
Alertmanager sends pages to Pushover and non-urgent alerts to email.
Disk usage alerts now fire at 90 percent instead of 80 percent.
Disk usage alerts fire at 80 percent.
The Kea DHCP lease time is 12 hours.
Static DHCP leases for servers are defined in the homelab repo, not on the router.
Home Assistant now runs as a VM on node006.
Home Assistant runs in Docker on ocean.
A Zigbee sensor in the kitchen warns when the fridge door is left open.
I learned Ansible mostly by writing the homelab playbooks.
The laptop is a MacBook Pro with 64 GB of RAM.
Local LLM inference on the laptop uses llama3.2:3b and qwen2.5:7b in ollama.
Qwen3 Coder 30B runs on node006 for local coding experiments.
Terminal bench results go into a Grafana dashboard.
The cat water fountains get cleaned every Sunday.
Ziggy and Pepper fight over the window perch.
Biscuit hides under the bed whenever the vacuum runs.
Mochi switched to a new hydrolysed protein brand because the old one was discontinued.
The MPC One's internal storage was replaced with a 1 TB SSD.
Sample packs live on nas01 under /mnt/data01/music/samples.
The bass on the Ocean Floor EP runs through a sidechain compressor keyed off the kick.
Kafka producers use acks=all with idempotence enabled.
Cruise Control generates the Kafka rebalance plans.
MirrorMaker 2 replicates the Kafka audit topics to the disaster recovery cluster.
The Kafka client upgrade to 3.7 is planned for next quarter.
Production Kafka runbooks live in the team wiki.
The new on-call rotation puts me on the Kafka platform every third week.
I use zsh with a minimal prompt.
Homebrew manages everything installed on the Mac.
The dotfiles repo is applied with a bootstrap script.
Claude Code sessions run in worktrees under .claude/worktrees.
Homelab secrets live in homelab/vault/secrets.yaml, encrypted with ansible-vault.
A leaked Plex token was found in a committed screenshot, so the git history was rewritten.
Tdarr's database lives on node006 local NVMe.
Sonarr was slow until its database moved off the NAS.
The arr stack updates itself weekly through Watchtower.
Watchtower was removed; container updates now go through Renovate PRs.
